solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Energy is absorbed by lucky chap

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken right inside another thing, so the first word goes within the second

blocks.note: 's is the clipped form of is, as in it's
Lucky Jim is the hero of Kingsley Amis's comic novel

explanation.surface: A fortunate fellow soaks up all the vitality around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' gives only S, from its short form 's. Lucky Jim, Kingsley Amis's 1954 novel, makes Jim the setters' standard lucky chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists this slang word in the sense of vigour or spirit, a less common meaning beside its vulgar one.

clue.text: Straightforward southern or northern bread

definitions.note: the bread means loaves, so plural

blocks.note: a dialect word for honest or fair
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A choice between plain loaves from the south or the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The same Lancashire dialect word means both honest and a loaf of oatmeal bread, so it is in the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In the north of England these are loaves of plain oaten bread, as recorded by Chambers.

clue.text: Heard swans and seals

indicators.note: heard means caught by the ear, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: young swans have a name sounding the same

explanation.surface: Someone listened to swans and seals, birds and marine animals together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seals' looks like the animals beside the swans; it means stamps for wax.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small seals, often on a ring, used to stamp official documents.

clue.text: Month with a person from Central America

blocks.note: a month of the year
taken as written

explanation.surface: A month spent with someone from Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maya are an indigenous people of Mexico and Central America, so one of them is such a person.

clue.text: Close to fibula, peasant hurt foot

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted
something hurt is damaged and bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the final letter of the leg bone's name
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A countryman has injured his foot, right by the fibula in his leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'foot' the injured body part; here it is a metrical foot in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a foot is a unit of rhythm, and this one has two short syllables followed by one long.

clue.text: Adult writings with anecdotes needed on Sabbath? Leave Mephisto!

blocks.note: A is the film certificate for adult
pages are written sheets
on and at both mean located by, as in on or at the door
ana are collections of anecdotes
surface padding: it sets the church scene and gives no letters

explanation.surface: Racy writings full of gossip need a stern sermon on Sunday telling the devil to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sabbath?' only sets the church scene. Mephisto is both the devil and this puzzle's name, a setter's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means 'get behind me, Satan', a command to the devil, and Mephisto is a devil.

clue.text: American fathers' holding out mostly for some wild sheep

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of it, so the word drops its last letter
holding means gripping inside, so the other pieces go around the shortened word

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
taken as written
dads are fathers

explanation.surface: American dads keep out most wild sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe on 'fathers'' is just surface; 'mostly' drops the last letter of 'out' before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Barbary sheep, wild animals of North Africa with long fringes of hair.

clue.text: Modern pubs I'm running as investments

indicators.note: running suggests moving about, so the letters are set in a different order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone running trendy bars treats them as investments.
explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are UK government savings bonds that pay out through a monthly prize draw instead of interest.
explanation.definitionFit: These government savings bonds are investments that pay out through prize draws rather than interest.

clue.text: In Paris love oddly is tense — as is this

definitions.note: this answer is itself a tense, so the clue's last words define it

indicators.note: oddly means taking only the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

blocks.note: the French word for love is amour
taken as written
T is an abbreviation for tense in grammar

explanation.surface: In Paris, love is strangely strained, a nervous city romance.
explanation.walkthrough: AMOUR, the French for love, gives its odd letters. The closing 'as is this' notes that the answer, like T, stands for a tense.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Greek verb tense expressing simple past action, so it too is a tense.

clue.text: Inactive rock group with a kind of rock

blocks.note: the Rolling Stones, the rock band
till is boulder clay left by glaciers

explanation.surface: A lazy rock band has a geology hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: Till is glacial boulder clay, a geologist's sense of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Motionless as a stone, totally unmoving, which is the sense of being inactive.

clue.text: One rejected Mediterranean port wine casks

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so the letter for one is removed

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
Tunis is the capital and port of Tunisia

explanation.surface: A North African port turns away one shipment of wine casks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuns are large barrels, historically used for storing wine or beer.

clue.text: Labour paranoid enthralling House — it's all the same to ministers

definitions.text: it's all the same to ministers

indicators.note: to labour is to work hard, and these letters are worked into a new order
enthralling means holding captive, so one part holds the other inside it

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A jittery Labour government has the House in its grip while ministers shrug that nothing makes any difference.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads Labour as the political party and ministers as government ones; the ministers are actually clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: In theology this Greek term names a matter of indifference, neither commanded nor forbidden, so churchmen may take either view.

clue.text: Hop it with box on fire close to Iowa, showing fear of dangerous stuff

indicators.note: something on fire is wildly agitated, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: part of the anagram fodder
the rest of the anagram fodder
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: Someone flees a burning box near Iowa, afraid of something hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' means next to here: the Iowa abbreviation goes straight after the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek-formed word names a morbid dread of poisons, which are dangerous substances.

clue.text: No dope taking ecstasy about to get reward

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the drug word holds the ecstasy letter inside it
turning about means facing the other way, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
dope is slang for a drug
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone is promised a prize for staying off drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: NO + DR(E)UG, then the whole string is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic poetic word means a recompense or prize, as found in Spenser and Shakespeare.

clue.text: Immature Edward holding duck and carp

indicators.note: holding means gripping something inside, so the short name goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: Ned is a short form of Edward
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, which looks like the letter O
to carp is to complain persistently, to nag

explanation.surface: A childish Edward is in charge of a duck and a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: N(O + NAG)ED: 'carp' looks like the fish, but it is the verb to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone not yet of legal age, a minor, and so not grown up.

clue.text: Lodgings in square, behind European river

indicators.note: behind says the first-named piece comes after the second one in the answer

blocks.note: the Inn flows through Switzerland, Austria and Germany
S is an abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: Somewhere to stay on a town square backing onto a river on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' puts the square's letter after the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are hostelries that offer travellers rooms for the night, which is what lodgings are.

clue.text: Neat round window? Elliptical actually

blocks.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
an eye is a small round opening or window

explanation.surface: Someone admires a tidy circular window, then corrects themselves: it is really oval.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, with the last two words correcting its shape. 'Neat' is not tidy but the archaic word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval dormer or lunette window in architecture is called by this name, like a bull's-eye opening.

clue.text: With churchman away, boy shows contempt in tirades

indicators.note: something away is gone, so these letters are taken out of the string

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
to diss is slang for to show disrespect
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a churchman's degree

explanation.surface: Once the vicar has left, a lad mocks him in angry rants.
explanation.walkthrough: LAD DISSES loses the DD where the two words meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A laisse is a stanza of an Old French chanson de geste, and Chambers also gives it as a tirade or long speech.

clue.text: Frank according to Will entertains with plonk in place of debauchery

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: plonk is cheap wine, here taken as wines
a sty is a filthy place of debauchery

explanation.surface: A frank man, so Shakespeare says, entertains guests with cheap wine in a den of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is Shakespeare, and 'Frank' is not a name but his noun for a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare used frank for a pen or sty where pigs are fattened, the same thing as this compound.

clue.text: Summons succeeded for lady about town

blocks.note: to cite someone is to summon them to court
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A woman out on the town is called to court and wins her case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about town' looks like a socialite; here it just means a female townsperson.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word for a female citizen means a woman of a city, hence a lady of the town.

clue.text: Respect is high for royal staff

indicators.note: being high suggests intoxicated and muddled, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Esteem for the palace employees runs high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal staff' looks like servants of a monarch; it is a single ceremonial rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch carries this ornamental rod as an emblem of sovereignty, literally a staff.

clue.text: Pretend agreement covers sleeping partner

indicators.note: something that covers wraps around another, so one word goes outside the other

blocks.note: a pact is an agreement
slang for someone one sleeps with

explanation.surface: A deal hides the existence of a silent business partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeping partner' looks like a passive investor in a firm, but it is a crude slang word for a bedfellow.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a show, behaving falsely as if in a play, is to pretend.

clue.text: Room high up overlooking a Greek region

blocks.note: an attic is a room under the roof
taken as written

explanation.surface: A room at the top of a house has a view over a part of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, overlooking means sitting above, so the room comes before the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Attica is the peninsula of Greece around Athens, a historic region of that country.

clue.text: Southern whisky in coloured glasses

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a malt is a malt whisky
i' is a clipped dialect form of in

explanation.surface: A southerner's whisky is poured into tinted tumblers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but supplies a letter: i' is a dialect form, as in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are pieces of coloured glass or enamel used in mosaic work; the singular is smalto.

clue.text: Supplier of shade and quiet, say

blocks.note: sh is the call for quiet
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Something offers shade and silence, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A window cover closed against sunlight keeps a room dim, so it provides shade.

clue.text: Boil fish of the cod family

blocks.note: first meaning: a blister or sore
second meaning: another name for the bib or pout

explanation.surface: Instructions to cook some cod-like fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boil' looks like a cooking order, but it is the noun meaning an inflamed swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an inflamed swelling on the skin and the pouting, a small fish related to cod.

clue.text: Polled in part of central England almost entirely

indicators.note: almost entirely means nearly all of it, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: Notts is short for Nottinghamshire, an English Midlands county

explanation.surface: Voters were canvassed across a region of the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polled' looks like opinion polling; it means having had the horns removed.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word describes cattle that are hornless or a head that is close-cropped, which is what polled means.

clue.text: Weed over in ditch I extracted

indicators.note: extracted means pulled out, so that letter is taken away
turned over in a down clue means flipped upside down, read the other way

blocks.note: a drain is a ditch
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pulling out weeds, someone toppled into a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' is a fair definition for any wild plant, here spikenard.
explanation.definitionFit: Spikenard is an aromatic plant, and a weed can be any wild herb.

clue.text: Hypothetical matter reportedly somehow missing red

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so those letters are taken out of the longer word
somehow suggests in some unspecified way, so the remaining letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the longer word, taken as written
the colour, taken as written, whose letters are removed

explanation.surface: Some theoretical stuff is said to be lacking its red component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it is fodder: remove R, E, D and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name given to a supposed primordial substance from which all chemical elements were thought to derive.

clue.text: Turn over case of yoghurts and trifles

indicators.note: the case of something is its outside, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: TO is the abbreviation for turnover, as in PTO
the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone flips a box of yoghurts and some trifles: a puddings scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifles' looks like the dessert alongside the yoghurts; it means things of little value.
explanation.definitionFit: Toys are playthings, so trifles of little worth, as in toying with something.

clue.text: Wormwood used in labs in Thailand

indicators.note: used in says the letters are employed within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A bitter herb is employed in laboratories in Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: This is another name for the wormwood plant, the herb that flavours the spirit absinthe.

clue.text: Go away packing cold ready-cooked chicken

indicators.note: packing means stuffing things inside, so the first word goes around the rest
something cooked has been prepared and changed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: scat is a command to clear off
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Instructions for leaving with some cold ready-cooked chicken in your bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready-cooked chicken' looks like a deli purchase; 'chicken' alone is the definition, meaning coward.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken is slang for a coward, and this childish phrase names someone easily frightened.

clue.text: Files circulating were located in place

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the word for place
circulating means going round, so the whole is turned the other way

blocks.note: things that sat somewhere were located there
stead means place, as in instead

explanation.surface: Documents being passed round had been kept in one spot.
explanation.walkthrough: STE(SAT)AD is read backwards. 'Files' here are computer files rather than folders.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of computer records are what a computing file holds, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Guy's theatrical? Not good

indicators.note: not good says the abbreviation for good must go from the word

blocks.note: stagy means theatrical or affected
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A man is a bit of a ham actor, and a poor one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man; it is a rope holding a mast or tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a supporting rope, and on a ship such a rope bracing a mast is also called by this word.
